model.rationale: The fundamentals-based baseline of a ~19-point Democratic margin rests on a solidly blue post-redistricting seat, and Solis's fundraising and outside-spending edge plus Polymarket pricing near 94% reinforce it. With no contrary evidence, I stay essentially at the baseline.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Solis could narrow the margin, though a Republican upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
California's 38th District is an open seat after redistricting created a new configuration, and no incumbent is on the ballot. The district leans Democratic by about eight points on the partisan vote index, and the baseline model combines that lean with a favorable national environment and a large money advantage to produce an expected Democratic margin near nineteen points.

Hilda Solis has raised over a million dollars and benefits from outside support, while Republican Pedro Casas reports no fundraising figures. Prediction markets give the Democratic candidate roughly a 94 percent chance of winning. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast relies on fundamentals, which point clearly toward a Safe Democratic outcome.
